html:
Kluane is the land around Kluane Lake in the southwest Yukon, home of the Kluane First Nation, a Southern Tutchone people based at Burwash Landing. They speak an Athabaskan language and are close kin of Champagne and Aishihik to the south.

They hunted sheep, moose and caribou, fished the lakes and traded with the coastal Tlingit, who brought goods over the mountain passes. The Klondike Gold Rush and a smaller rush at Kluane Lake in 1903 brought the first wave of outsiders. In 1942 the US Army built the Alaska Highway along the lake, and in 1943 a game sanctuary, later Kluane National Park, closed much of their hunting land. The First Nation signed a land claim agreement in 2003.
